Investment Structure Lifecycle Decision Tool

Build single-owner or true split-sleeve pathways. Each bond, long-term equity and high-turnover sleeve can use its own owner, funding action, wrapper, additions, access method and exit. All rates and dollar results are editable planning sensitivities—not legal, tax, investment, insurance or surety conclusions.

How to use: select one card in each phase. Phase 1 contains both “keep” and every “move” action. A selected card can be deselected by clicking it again. Impossible later choices stay visible but collapse and turn gray. Minimize keeps a labeled title bar with a restore button. Pin the current pathway to keep it in the frozen comparison strip.
Pinned pathways remain editable: load one back into the builder, remove it, or reorder it in the frozen strip. The ranked table uses value before distribution, ROI, value after distribution, value before estate tax and value after estate tax.

Ranked lifecycle pathways

Bond, long-term equity and high-turnover consequences

Responsive projections: the input panel stacks above results on narrow screens. Rows distinguish bond interest, dividends, realized gains, BPT, financing, PPLI, distributions and estate tax. Single-owner taxable/PPLI cases and a split-entity case are shown separately.

Projection paths

Lifecycle ranking

Year-by-year tax and cash-flow rows

Current-year BPT by receipt category

Gates govern specific actions; they are not vague checklist items. Each card states the governed actions, evidence required, failure consequence and connected assumptions. Changing a gate or control recalculates the builder and projections.
All 67 source-model scenario families remain available. Each row retains the source funding, current-tax, distribution, estate and exit information.
Latest workbooks, Word comparisons, adviser responses, reserve/surety documents, OCR trust text and the relevant reserve email are preserved for audit. Document text is intentionally not auto-linked, preventing “CTI” from appearing inside unrelated words such as “extraction.”

Source sets
Plain-language definitions explain what each term means, why it matters here, and the cited authority. Statutory quotations are marked as condensed when they are not verbatim full text.

Independent accuracy review

Use boundary. This is a planning and sensitivity tool, not a tax return, valuation, legal opinion, investment recommendation, insurance illustration, or surety consent. Numeric rankings remain conditional on the gates shown in the tool.

Verdict on the red-team findings

FindingIndependent verdictDisposition
Current-year CTI E&P omitted from beneficiary accessConfirmed. The prior access engine added opening E&P and only the separate flat E&P-build input.Corrected with a year-by-year E&P ledger and §301/§316 ordering.
Property distribution lacks §311(b)/§312Confirmed. The former pathway had no FMV/inside-basis gate and returned no corporate gain.Corrected; unconfirmed basis blocks ranking.
CTI hold-to-death taxes unrealized inside gainConfirmed as a conceptual defect in the generic death label. Death is not a deemed corporate asset sale.Split into heirs-hold, stepped-up-stock sale, and post-death inside asset sale/liquidation.
Sale/loan estate includes entire trust valueConfirmed. Creditor note/payments and trust equity require separate balance sheets.Corrected when the completed-gift/estate-opinion gate passes.
Guam military-contract BPT descriptionConfirmed inaccurate. Current 11 GCA §26202 contains the over-$10M, DoD-or-foreign-government and aggregate phased/modified-contract formulation.Text corrected and kept separate from portfolio-income BPT.
Scenarios 24 and 41 silently use stale SBLOC figuresConfirmed. The prior getter returned stored figures after calculation failure.Stored numbers are suppressed while the SBLOC gate is open.
CTI DRD categorically missingPartly confirmed, but the proposed universal correction would be wrong. The operating plan records EY's Nov. 6, 2026 position that CTI receives no §243 deduction because U.S. companies are foreign for Guam-tax purposes; it also records §881(b) treatment with no 30% withholding.Added a gated DRD sensitivity, default OFF to EY's documented position.
Partnership, CLAT, lender interest, 2026 label, ROIConfirmed.Partner-level profile, CLAT gift-rate source, creditor-side estate schedule, forward-period labels and CAGR relabeling added.
PHC/AET, real estate, gift source, DAPT, ILIT, QOF, flat ratesConfirmed as scope/label limitations.Labels and ranking gates narrowed to the implemented sensitivities.

Document-confirmed facts used in the model

  • The Nov. 13, 2026 operating plan records EY's preliminary 2025 CTI E&P of approximately $52 million and Core Tech Trust stock basis of approximately $13.785 million; those remain editable, preliminary inputs.
  • The same plan records EY's position of no §243 deduction for CTI and qualification under §881(b) with no 30% withholding. DRD therefore defaults OFF.
  • The full 34-page Eun Family Investment Trust deed is present inside the Outlook message. Article I(A) states §2503(b) intent; Article I(D) says irrevocable; Article III bars distributions before Jan. 1, 2017 and thereafter gives the Independent Trustees discretion; Article VII(E) uses the §672(c) related/subordinate restriction; Article VII(J) bars removal/appointment attribution; Article VIII(A)(7) restricts §2042 incidents of ownership; Article VIII(F) authorizes QSST/ESBT elections; Article VIII(J) bars grantor-tax reimbursement unless the Independent Trustees later amend under the stated estate-inclusion condition.
  • Article XIV of the deed overrides Article I(D) and reserved a revocation/amendment power until the earlier of April 30, 2015 or written relinquishment. The attached First Amendment states that power had been retained, then deletes Article XIV and relinquishes it. The attached Second Amendment names Ho Sang Eun as initial Family Trustee and Conchita D. Bathan as initial Independent Trustee.
  • The 2025 Guam Form 1041 is marked complex trust, not grantor-type trust, and names Ho Eun as trustee. It reports $434,854 taxable income, including $424,101 short-term capital gain, $174,813 total tax and $15,930 NIIT. The return package supports a separate professional review of trustee status, grantor-trust classification, QC compliance and any third-party payment of the trust's tax.
  • The Core Tech Trust First Amendment identifies Ho Eun and Hui Eun as settlors and Ho Eun as sole and initial trustee.
  • QC S-14-001 shows an effective date of Dec. 10, 2014 and expiration Dec. 10, 2034. The 2025 Certificate of Compliance states a 100% income-tax rebate for trust earnings within its terms.

Open assumptions and mandatory professional-review items

  • Possible constructive dividend or gift: the supplied context reports that CTI check #18383 paid the trust's $174,813 tax. The OCR of the 28-page return confirms the liability but did not independently recover that check image/number. Treat the payment characterization as unresolved until the check, ledger entry and authority are reviewed.
  • Trust classification: the 2025 complex-trust filing, Ho Eun trustee disclosure, the Second Amendment naming Ho Sang Eun Family Trustee, deed powers and GEDA requirements must be reconciled by Guam/U.S. trust counsel and the return preparer. The tool does not infer a final grantor/foreign/domestic or estate-exclusion conclusion.
  • CPMA: the PDF's embedded text is font-encoded and garbled. OCR was embedded as a convenience but is not reliable for clause-level contract analysis. Obtain a clean text/searchable copy before using covenant language.
  • Real estate: adjusted basis, depreciation method, passive-loss carryforwards, §1250/unrecaptured §1250 and terminal recapture are not computed; those paths stay outside winner rankings unless the gate is confirmed.
  • PHC/AET: modeled charges are sensitivities, not exact computations of adjusted ordinary gross income, undistributed PHC income, accumulated taxable income, dividends-paid deductions, credits or reasonable-business-needs adjustments.
  • Rates: individual, trust, partner, beneficiary and state taxes remain flat-rate planning inputs; brackets, character, sourcing, residence, deductions and return-level limitations can change outcomes.

ARTICLE 1.
TAX REBATES

Grant of Benefits
[§§58128.6(a) & (b), QC Law]
§1.01. THIS IS TO CERTIFY that the EUN FAMILY INVESTMENT TRUST (the "Guam-based Trust"), a .
trust created and existing under and by virtue of the laws of the United States, and administered in Guam
by Ms. Hui_Eun, have qualified for and are hereby GRANTED the rebates set out in this Article 1 of income
tax payable to the government of Guam, all pursuant to Chapter 58, Title 12, Guam Code Annotated as amended
by P.L. 24-266 and P.L. 25-08 and P.L. 25-150 (the "QC Law").

Income tax rebate; renewal

[§58128.6(a), QC Law]
§1.02. The Guam-based Trust shall be entitled to a rebate of one hundred percent (100%) of all income tax
paid by the Guam-based Trust to the government of Guam on all its earnings, including investments, from
inside or outside of Guam, for a period of twenty (20) years from the effective date of this special qualifying
certificate ("Special QC"). This Special QC may be renewed by applying to the Guam Economic
Development Authority ("GEDA") for additional periods of twenty (20) years at the conclusion of the first
or subsequent periods as long as the Guam-based Trust remains in good standing under the laws of Guam
and under the rules and regulations of GEDA. The taxable income of the Guam-based Trust shall be computed
generally in the same manner of an individual in which the deductions and credits allowed to an individual are
also allowed to the Guam-based Trust, as provided in section 641(b) of the tax code and the exceptions
thereto. For purposes of sections 641 and 935 of the Internal Revenue Code and of the Guam Territorial
income tax, the Guam-based Trust shall be treated as an individual who is a citizen of the United States but a
resident of Guam.

Rebate of income tax withheld on dividends; renewal
[§58128.6(b), QC Law]
§1.03. The Non-Resident Beneficiary shall be entitled to a rebate of one hundred percent (100%) of the
income tax withheld from them on the payments or distributions made by the Guam-based Trust, for a period
of twenty (20) consecutive years from the effective date of the Special QC, provided, the payments or
distributions were/are subject to withholding tax. This period of rebate for the Non-Resident Beneficiary may
be renewed for additional periods of twenty (20) years at the conclusion of the first or subsequent periods so
long as the Guam-based Trust remains in good standing under the laws of Guam and under the rules and
regulations of GEDA. 6

OF) 124 4752

===== PAGE 15 =====
ARTICLE 2.
AUTHORITY FOR ISSUANCE

Non-Transferable
[§§58121, 58128.6(c) QC Law]

§2.01. This Special QC is issued upon ascertaining that the materials furnished by the Trustee on behalf of the
Guam-based Trust are in proper order, and that the appropriate fees have been paid. Neither this Special QC
nor its benefits may be /ransferred, assigned, or conveyed to another trustee without the written permission of
GEDA being first obtained. For purposes of this Certificate, a "transfer of benefits" shall have occurred at
any time that (i) there is a transfer of a majority of the voting stock of, or ownership interest in the Guam-
based Trust resulting in a change in the identity of the Non-Resident Beneficiary who or which control the
Guam-based Trust, or (ii) the Guam-based Trust shall lease, assign or transfer a substantial part of its
activities or assets outside of the ordinary course of its business.

ARTICLE 3. CONDITIONS

Compliance mandatory
[§§58103, 58135, QC Law]
§3.01. This Special QC is issued in reliance and is conditioned upon the truth and accuracy of the
representations contained in the application of the Guam-based Trust, including all exhibits thereto, and is
further conditioned upon compliance with the terms and limitations set out in this Special QC and in the QC
Law.

Compliance with laws, rules, and regulations
[§58111, QC Law]

§3.02. The Guam-based Trust, its Non-Resident Beneficiary, and its Trustee shall comply with all of the
laws of Guam, specifically the QC Law, the Guam Trust Incentives Act, and the Guam Trust Companies Act
and, all the laws of the United States applicable to such Trust activities, and the rules and regulations of its
various agencies, including but not limited to those set out in the QC Law, and in the rules and regulations of
GEDA and the Department of Revenue and

Taxation.

Effective date of Special QC
[§58101, QC Law]
§3.03. The effective date of this Special QC and the tax rebates provided for in Article I, supra, shall be the
date of approval of this instrument executed in writing by the Governor of Guam.

Annual reports
[§8.01 GEDA Rules and Regulations for Trusts and §3 Department of
Revenue & Taxation Rules & Regulations for Trusts]
§3.04. The Trustee shall furnish to the Authority no later than August 15th of each year, a copy of its Annual
Report of the Non-Resident Beneficiary's Trust to its Trustor, to include: (1) the corpus of the Guam-based
trust at the beginning of the year, (2) annual earnings of the trust, (3) payments to the Non-Resident
Beneficiary, (4) the corpus of the Guam-based trust at the end of the year, and (5) any change in the account
during the year. Alternatively, in the case of a trust company serving as trustee, a copy of the annual statement
filed with the Commissioner of Banking of the government of Guam, as required in §160304 of Chapter

Ly

160. Title 11 Guam Code Annotated (GCA). may be filed with the Authority.

Use of Guam financial institutions
[§160302, Chapter 160, Title 11 GCA; §4.4, Department of
Revenue & Taxation Rules & Regulations for Trusts]

§3.05. All funds in the Guam-based Trust shall be deposited in a Guam financial institution. The Trustee
shall have an office on Guam in which it maintains its business and corporate records and financial books. The
Trustee may establish its principle office on Guam in office space that it shares with other businesses,
including other trust companies or affiliates, provided, that the office equipment, corporate records, and
financial books of accounts of the Trustee are kept separate and distinct from those of other businesses,
including other trust companies or affiliates.

Certificate of compliance
[§58135, QC Law]
§3.06. GEDA shall certify to the Department of Revenue and Taxation the compliance by the Guam-based
Trust and by the Non-Resident Beneficiary with the terms and conditions of this Special QC and with the QC
Law. GEDA's certification mus! accompany any request for a tax rebate made to the Department of Revenue
and Taxation by the Guam-based Trust or by its Non-Resident Beneficiary.

Submission of Proof of Custodial Receipt
[§5.01 GEDA Rules and Regulations for Trust]
§3.07. The Trustee shall furnish to GEDA no later than 90 days after the effective date of this QC, proof of
custodial receipt of the corpus of the Guam-based Trust by a bank, a trust company, or other financial service
establishment, licensed by the Guam Department of Revenue and Taxation to provide financial and trust services
within the territory of Guam. The proof of custodial receipt required to be furnished pursuant to this section
shall be in a form acceptable to GEDA.

No Representation as to Eligibility for Tax Benefits

§3.08. GEDA, in recommending issuance of this Special QC, and the Government of Guam, in issuing this
Special QC, offer no opinions and make no representations or warranties as to whether any rebates granted under
this Special QC, or the income realized by the Guam-based Trust, the Non-Resident Beneficiary(ies), or the
Trustee which may be eligible for the rebates granted under this Special QC, are exempt from any reporting
requirements or from taxation under the laws of the United States, any State of the United States, any other
political subdivision of the United States, or any foreign government. By accepting this Special QC, the
Guam-based Trust, the Non-Resident Beneficary(ies), the Trustee, and the Trustor represent that they have
relied upon the advice of their own legal counsel and tax advisors in submitting the application for, and in
accepting, this Special QC.

False representations

QC or for any amendments thereto shall be subsequently determined by GEDA to have been false, then this
Special QC shall be void ab initio.

Non-complignce
[§58111(b), QC Law]

this Special QC must be in writing and in full compliance with the QC Law, Chapter 160 of Title 11, GCA.
and with the rules and regulations of GEDA and the Department of Revenue and Taxation.

General grounds for revocation

APPENDIX                ·    WHY THE BELL LADDER



22 years of evidence, one sentence of logic
A reserve's real risk is reinvestment risk: cash re-earns whatever the Fed sets, while a bell ladder reinvests only the slice that matures each year.




    +54bp / yr                                                                               1.16% vs 0.04%                                            $3.49M vs $2.26M

    0–5 yr bell vs. cash, 2005–2026, with about half                                         worst single year of book yield — bell vs. cash.          income per $100M in year 3 after a 200bp Fed cut
    the income volatility (1.04 vs 1.96)                                                     Cash paid ~zero for 8 of 22 years                         — the bell holds its income, cash does not




The trade-off, stated plainly: ~2.4 years of duration means a +300bp shock marks the portfolio down ~6.8% on paper. The mark is temporary — every bond pulls to par, and
annual maturities reinvest at the new higher rates. Full backtest and trade-off detail in the companion deck.

     The QC rewrites the playbook. Per the Certificate of Compliance (benefit year 2025, certified 3/25/2026): a 100% rebate of the Guam income tax the trust pays on its earnings —
     including investment income from inside or outside Guam — through December 10, 2034, plus a 100% rebate of withholding on dividends to non-resident beneficiaries,
     renewable for further 20-year periods. The rebate covers Guam income tax only; it does not remove federal tax. If the trust is a foreign grantor trust, the owner still
     pays federal tax on its income; if it is a non-grantor trust, the trust is itself taxed federally: as a domestic trust at trust rates, or as a foreign trust on U.S.-source income (30% on U.S. dividends in the tool's what-if; portfolio interest and most gains only if the exemption conditions are met). The withholding rebate covers payments from this trust to non-resident
     beneficiaries, not a CTI dividend paid to a mainland trust, which is a separate payment the certificate may not reach. The question for CPA and counsel is the funding
     path from CTI into the irrevocable trust and the trust's federal status.




QC S-14-001 (executed 11/12/2014; effective 12/10/2014, expires 12/10/2034; compliance certified 3/25/2026). Key conditions: funds at a Guam-licensed financial institution (§3.05, §3.07); annual GEDA reporting (§3.04); benefits non-transferable
(§2.01). Trust documents (10/16/2014 agreement; 2nd Amendment Oct 2025, GEDA-filed) show Ho Sang Eun as grantor and, since Oct 2025, Family Trustee — possible grantor-trust treatment could tax trust income to the grantor directly, bypassing the
trust-level rebate, and the trustee change may require GEDA's §2.01 written permission. Counsel and EY to confirm. Illustrative yields: 5.6% taxable IG, 3.7% muni blend. Not tax advice.

Summary for Surety Review
BG Investment Services, LLC (an ASC Trust, LLC company) · Updated November 10, 2026 · Confidential — prepared at the request of
Core Tech International

Purpose
Core Tech International (CTI) is engaging BG Investment Services, LLC (“BGIS”), an SEC-registered investment
adviser, to manage approximately $100 million of reserves, beginning with approximately $90 million currently at
First Hawaiian Bank. The program pairs a laddered bond portfolio, which serves as the liquidity engine, with an
equity growth allocation that starts small and grows over time. As discussed with CTI’s surety representatives, no
marketable investment — including short-term bonds or structured notes — guarantees principal; this program
manages risk through quality, diversification, liquidity and discipline, and is designed so the liquidity and credit
strength supporting CTI’s bonding capacity are preserved.

Which entity holds the program
CTI is finalizing, with its CPA (EY), which Core Tech entity will hold the program. Accounts are being opened for all
three so funds can move once the choice is made. The investment program — allocation, guardrails, custody and
reporting — is the same whichever entity holds it.

 Entity                             How funded                                     On CTI’s balance sheet
 Core Tech International (CTI)      Already holds the cash — no transfer           The investments
 Core Tech Trust (Mr. Ho’s          Documented loan from CTI                       A note receivable from the trust
 revocable trust)
 Eun Family Investment Trust        Documented loan from CTI                       A note receivable from the trust
 (GEDA Qualifying Certificate S-
 14-001)


How the funds move
 1. Today: the cash is held by CTI (approximately $90 million, at First Hawaiian Bank).
 2. Entity decision: CTI selects the holding entity. If it is Core Tech Trust or the Eun Family Investment Trust, CTI
    transfers the funds as a documented loan (for the Eun Family Investment Trust, through its account at Bank
    of Guam).
 3. Investment account: a Fidelity Investments account managed by BGIS in the chosen entity’s name; for the
    Eun Family Investment Trust, titled ASC Trust, LLC (a Guam-licensed trust company) FBO the Trust. Funds are
    held in money market and U.S. Treasuries.
 4. After consent (expected week of November 16): with the bond agent’s and sureties’ consent, the portfolio is
    invested gradually at 80% bonds / 20% equity.
 5. Ongoing: each month or quarter, cash above CTI’s $100–120 million operating balance at First Hawaiian Bank
    is added to the program.

What the program holds
  • Initial allocation: 80% bonds / 20% stocks. Planned glide, subject to the sureties’ consent: a reverse target-
    date path as the focus shifts to long-term family wealth — about 60% stocks in 2027, about 80% in 2028 and
    about 90% from 2029. Each step is gradual, reviewed quarterly and communicated.
  • Bonds at full glide: about 9–10% of the program stays in the bond ladder — roughly $60 million in 2029,
    growing with the program to about $110 million by 2032.
  • Equity allocation: individually owned large-capitalization, blue chip U.S. stocks, broadly diversified with
    position limits, built gradually in quarterly tranches. Daily liquid; no lockups.
  • Bond portfolio — the liquidity engine: a laddered portfolio of U.S. Treasuries and investment-grade corporate
    bonds, maturities 0–5 years, portfolio average credit quality A-, BBB- limited to 5%, no issuer above 2%,
    average duration approximately 2.4 years. All securities can be sold with next-day settlement.
  • No leverage, no margin, no derivatives, no illiquid or private holdings in the program. Assets are unpledged
    and unencumbered.

Liquidity outside the program
  • CTI keeps $100–120 million of operating cash at First Hawaiian Bank outside this program; only cash above
    that level is added.
  • CTI’s $50 million line of credit with First Hawaiian Bank is up for renewal.
  • Per CTI management, the company's cash position is projected to grow from approximately $238 million
    today to approximately $630 million by December 2028 — with a plan to reach approximately $1 billion in
    cash or cash equivalents by 2032 — from operating earnings and project-level financings that are self-
    liquidating under debt-service coverage requirements. CTI and its construction entities carry no debt.

Governance and reporting
  • A written Investment Policy Statement with allocation ranges, equity position limits, duration and credit-
    quality guardrails, executed before funding.
  • Quarterly reporting including an equity drawdown scenario, an interest-rate stress test (+300bp mark-to-
    market), and a 12-month maturity schedule mapped against planned cash needs. Copies can be made
    available to the surety on request.
  • BGIS is a registered investment adviser; advisory fees are disclosed separately and are not deducted from
    reported yields without disclosure.

Balance sheet and titling
Until funds move, the cash is on CTI’s balance sheet. If CTI holds the program, the investments stay on CTI’s
balance sheet. If Core Tech Trust or the Eun Family Investment Trust holds it, the investments are titled to that
trust and CTI’s balance sheet carries a note receivable for the loan. The entity and loan terms are being confirmed
with CTI’s CPA (EY) and counsel, and the choice — and any later change — will be communicated to the surety.

Contact: Paul Ma, CFA, Chief Strategist, BG Investment Services, LLC · pm@bg-investments.com · (617) 905-6672 · Maree Pelkey
Sgro, CFP®, AIF®, Executive Vice President · (671) 472-5141
This summary is for informational purposes in connection with CTI’s surety relationship and is not investment, legal or tax advice. Figures are
indicative as of November 2026 and subject to the final Investment Policy Statement.

(B) Trust Administrative Provisions. In the administration of all trusts hereunder:

which may require impartiality as among such interests, and the interests of all subsequent

favor of beneficiaries of the trust in the absence of affirmative reasons (including tax reasons) for

be required to, inquire into or take into account the other income or resources of any beneficiary
or the obligation of any person to support any beneficiary.

BGIS

BG INVESTMENT SERVICES, LLC

AN ASC TRUST, LLC COMPANY

COMPREHENSIVE PORTFOLIO MANAGEMENT AGREEMENT

Client Name: Core Tech International Corporation

This Agreement is made effective as of between the undersigned party (hereinafter
referred to as the “Client”) and BG Investment Services, LLC. (“BGIS”), a Registered Investment Adviser
located at 120 Father Duenas Avenue, Hagatfia, Guam 96910 (collectively referred to as the “Parties”).

1. SCOPE OF ENGAGEMENT.

Discretionary Management

Client hereby appoints BGIS as the Investment Adviser to perform the services hereinafter described. BGIS
accepts such appointment. BGIS shall be responsible for discretionary investment and reinvestment of those
Assets designated by the Client on Schedule A to be subject to BGIS’s management (the “Assets” or “Account”).
BGIS is authorized, without prior consultation with the Client, to buy, sell, and trade in stocks, bonds, mutual
funds, and other securities and/or contracts relating to the same. Unless otherwise agreed to by both Parties,
any subsequently opened Accounts shall be governed by this Agreement. The authority granted to BGIS herein
shall continue in force until revoked by the Client in writing. Such revocation shall be effective upon receipt by
BGIS.

(a) As part of the Comprehensive Portfolio Management Service, Client will be provided asset management and
financial planning or consulting services fora single fee. This service is designed to assist Client in meeting their
financial goals through the use of a financial plan or consultation. Client meetings will be conducted to understand
Client's current financial situation, existing resources, financial goals, and tolerance for risk. Based on what is
learned, an investment approach is presented, including, but not limited to, individual stocks, bonds, exchange
traded funds (“ETFs”), options, mutual funds and/or other public and private securities or investments. Once the
appropriate portfolio has been determined, portfolios are continuously and regularly monitored, and if necessary,
rebalanced based upon client's individual needs, stated goals and objectives. Upon client request, BGIS will provide
a summary of observations and recommendations for the planning or consulting aspects of this service.

BGIS may use the sub-advisory services of a third-party investment advisory firm (“Sub-Adviser”) to aid in the
implementation of an investment portfolio. Before selecting a Sub-Adviser, BGIS will ensure that the chosen
party is properly licensed or registered.

(b) BGIS’s management personnel or financial advisors review accounts on at least an annual basis. The nature
of these reviews is to learn whether the Client's accounts are in line with their investment objectives,
appropriately positioned based on market conditions, and investment policies, if applicable. Accounts managed
by a third party manager are reviewed on atleast an annual basis. BGIS does not provide written reports. Verbal
reports take place on at least an annual basis when Clients are contacted. BGIS may review Client Accounts
more frequently than described above, based on major market or economic events, the Client's life events,
requests by the Client, etc.

(c) BGIS believes that the annual fee assessed in Section 2 is reasonable in relation to (1) the advisory services
provided under this Agreement; and (2) the fees charged by other investment advisers offering similar
services /programs.

(d) Client agrees to provide information and/or documentation requested by BGIS in furtherance of services
provided under this Agreement as it pertains to the Client's income, investments, taxes, insurance, estate plan,
etc. Client also agrees to discuss specific investment objectives, needs and goals with BGIS, and to keep BGIS
informed of any changes regarding the aforementioned items. Client acknowledges that BGIS cannot
adequately perform services unless Client diligently performs their responsibilities under this Agreement. BGIS
shall not be required to verify any information obtained from the Client, Client's attorney, accountant or other
professionals, and is expressly authorized to rely thereon.

Pagel

===== PAGE 2 =====
2. ADVISER COMPENSATION.

The maximum annual fee charged for this service will not exceed 1.50%. Fees to be assessed will be outlined
in Schedule A of this Agreement. Annualized fees are billed on a pro-rata basis quarterly in advance based on
the value of the account(s) on the last day of the previous quarter. Fees will be deducted from Client
account(s) by BGIS and/or the chosen Sub-Adviser. Adjustments will be made for deposits and withdrawals
during the quarter that exceed 10% of Client's account value. BGIS does not offer direct invoicing. As part of
this process, Clients understand the following:

(a) Client provides authorization permitting BGIS, Sub-Adviser to be directly paid by these terms.; and

(b) Client's independent custodian sends statements, at least quarterly, showing the market values for
each security included in the Assets and all account disbursements, including the amount of the
advisory fees paid to BGIS; and

(c) BGIS will send an invoice directly to the custodian. If BGIS sends an invoice to the Client, a legend urging
the comparison of information provided in the statement with those from the qualified custodian will
be included.

BGIS shall never have custody except for authorized fee withdrawal of Client funds or securities and third party
money movement authority, as the services of a qualified and independent custodian will be used. BGIS
generally invests Client's cash balances in money market funds, FDIC Insured Certificates of Deposit, high-grade
commercial paper and/or government backed debt instruments. Ultimately, BGIS will try to achieve the highest
return on Client cash balances through relatively low-risk and conservative investments. In most cases, at least
a partial cash balance will be maintained in a money market account so that BGIS may debit advisory fees for
services rendered.

The fees charged are calculated as described above, and are not charged on the basis of a share of capital gains
upon, or capital appreciation of, the funds, or any portion of the funds of an advisory Client (15 U.S.C. §80b-
5(a)(1))-

3. DIRECTIONS TO BGIS.

Except for decisions regarding the purchase and/or sale of specific investments, all directions from the Client
to BGIS (i.e. notices, instructions, including directions relating to changes in the Client's investment objectives)
shall be in writing and shall be effective upon receipt by BGIS. BGIS shall be fully protected in relying upon any
such direction, notice, or instruction until it has been duly advised in writing of changes therein.

Client has the opportunity to place reasonable restrictions on the types of investments to be held in the portfolio.
Restrictions on investments in certain securities or types of securities may not be possible due to the level of
difficulty this would entail in managing the account.

4. DISCLOSURE STATEMENT.

Client acknowledges receipt of BGIS’s Form ADV Part 2 and Privacy Policy at or before the time of signing this
Agreement in accordance with Rule 204-3 under the Investment Advisers Act of 1940. In addition, Client
acknowledges receipt of BGIS’s Form CRS at or before the time of signing this Agreement in accordance with
Rule 204-5 under the Investment Advisers Act of 1940 if Client is a natural person, or the legal representative
of such natural person, who seeks to receive or receives services primarily for personal, family, or household
purposes. Client acknowledges and consents to BGIS sending these disclosure statements in electronic format
to the email address(es) provided by Client.

7. BROKER-DEALER/CUSTODIAN & EXECUTION OF TRANSACTIONS.

The Assets are not held by BGIS. The Assets shall be held by a qualified custodian (“Custodian”). BGIS is
authorized to give instructions to the Custodian with respect to all investment decisions regarding the Assets.
Client authorizes and directs the Custodian to effect transactions, deliver securities, make payments and
otherwise take such actions as BGIS shall direct in connection with BGIS’s management of the Assets outlined
in Section 1.

Client acknowledges and agrees that in order to discharge the responsibilities outlined in Section 1 of this
Agreement, all securities transactions must be affected through a Custodian. BGIS must arrange to execute
securities transactions for the Assets through a Custodian that will reasonably provide “best execution”. In
seeking best execution, the determining factor is not the lowest possible commission cost but whether the
transaction represents the best qualitative execution for the Client. BGIS takes into consideration the full range
of an independent custodian’s services, including the value of research provided, execution capability,
transaction costs, commission rates, other applicable fees, and responsiveness. BGIS will seek to provide the
Client with access to competitive commission rates but may not necessarily obtain the lowest possible
commission rates for applicable transactions. It is important to note that BGIS does not have discretion to
negotiate commission rates with a Custodian. The brokerage commissions and/or transaction fees charged to
the Client by a Custodian for securities transactions ARE included within BGIS’s compensation outlined in
Section 2 of this Agreement. BGIS does not receive any portion of the fees charged by the Custodian.

Client may also pay holdings charges imposed by the Custodian for certain investments, charges imposed
directly by a mutual fund, index fund, or exchange traded fund, which shall be disclosed in the fund's
prospectus (e.g, fund management fees), distribution fees, surrender charges, variable annuity fees, IRA
and qualified retirement plan fees, mark-ups and mark-downs, spreads paid to market makers, fees for trades
executed away from Client's Custodian, wire transfer fees, and other fees and taxes on brokerage accounts
and securities transactions.

BGIS generally processes transactions for each Client account independently, unless BGIS decides to purchase

Page 3

===== PAGE 4 =====
or sell the same securities for several Clients at approximately the same time. BGIS may (but is not obligated
to) combine or “batch” orders for a variety of factors, including but not limited to, obtaining best execution for
all parties. Under this procedure, the transaction price will be averaged, and securities will be allocated among
BGIS’s Clients in proportion to the purchase and sale orders placed for each Client account on any given day.

8. NON-EXCLUSIVE MANAGEMENT.

BGIS, its officers, employees, and agents, may have or take the same or similar positions in specific investments
for their own accounts, or for the accounts of other clients, as BGIS does for the Client's Assets. Client expressly
acknowledges and understands that BGIS shall be free to render investment advice to others and that BGIS
does not make investment management services available exclusively to the Client. Nothing in this Agreement
shall put BGIS under any obligation to purchase or sell, or to recommend for purchase or sale for any Client
account, any securities which BGIS, BGIS employees, affiliates, representatives, or agents, may purchase or sell
for themselves or for the account of any other client, unless in BGIS’s determination, such investment would be
in the best interest of the Client.

9. RISKACKNOWLEDGMENT.

BGIS does not guarantee the future performance of the Assets or any specific level of performance, the success
of any investment decision or strategy used, or the success of BGIS’s overall management of the Assets. Client
understands that investment decisions made for the Assets by BGIS are subject to various markets, currency,
economic, political, and business risks, and that those investment decisions will not always be profitable.

10. PROXIES.
Client acknowledges that BGIS will not vote proxies.

11. ASSIGNMENT.

This Agreement may not be assigned (within the meaning of the Advisers Act) by either Party without the prior
consent of the other Party. Client acknowledges and agrees that transactions that do not result in a change of
actual control or management of BGIS shall not be considered an assignment pursuant to Rule 202(a)(1)-1
under the Advisers Act.

12. TERMINATION.

Either Party may terminate this Agreement in writing at any time. Upon receipt of notice of termination, BGIS
will process a pro-rata refund of the unearned portion of the advisory fees charged in advance at the beginning
of the quarter.

13. DEATH OR DISABILITY.

The death or incapacity of the Client shall not terminate the authority of BGIS granted herein until BGIS receives
notice of such death or incapacity. Upon such notice the Client’s executor, guardian, attorney-in-fact or other
authorized representative must engage BGIS in order to continue to provide services to the Assets.

14. ARBITRATION.

This Agreement supersedes any and all preexisting agreements and/or understandings. This
Agreement contains a provision, which requires that all claims arising out of transactions or activities
affecting the provision of services by BGIS to the Client be resolved through arbitration. To the extent
permitted by law, all controversies which may arise between the Parties or any of their affiliated
companies concerning any transaction arising out of or relating to this Agreement, or the construction,
performance, or breach of this or any other agreement between the Parties, whether entered into prior to, on
or subsequent to the date hereto, shall be submitted to arbitration conducted under the Rules of the
American Arbitration Association. Arbitration must be commenced by service upon the other Party, of a
written demand for arbitration or a written notice of intention to arbitrate. Judgment upon any award
rendered by the arbitrator(s) shall be final and may be entered in any court having jurisdiction. The Parties
hereby submit to the in personam jurisdiction

===== PAGE 5 =====
of the courts of the Guam and the local courts located therein (“Chosen Jurisdiction”) (and expressly waive any
defense to personal jurisdiction of the Client by such courts) for the purpose of confirming, vacating, or
modifying any such award or judgment entered thereon. Service of process in such action shall be sufficient if
served on the Parties by certified mail, return receipt requested, at the last address known to the other Party.
In this connection the Parties expressly waive any defense(s) to personal jurisdiction of the Parties by such
court; to service of process as set forth above; to venue; and in addition, expressly agree that the Chosen
Jurisdiction is a convenient forum for any such action.

Nothing herein shall be enforceable to the extent that the Client waives their rights under state or federal
securities laws. The Parties acknowledge, understand and agree that: (i) Arbitration is final and binding on the
Parties; (ii) The Parties are waiving their right to seek remedies in court, including the right to jury trial; (iii)
Pre-arbitration discovery is generally more limited than and potentially different in form and scope from court
proceedings; (iv) The Arbitration Award is not required to include factual findings or legal reasoning and any
Party's right to appeal or to seek modification of a ruling by the arbitrators is strictly limited; and (v) The panel
of arbitrators will typically include a minority of arbitrators who were or are affiliated with the securities
industry.

No person shall bring a putative or certified class action to arbitration, nor seek to enforce any pre-dispute
arbitration agreement against any person who has initiated in court a putative class action; or is a member of
a putative class who has not opted out of the class with respect to any claims encompassed by the putative class
action until: (i) the class certification is denied; or (ii) the class is decertified; or (iii) the customer is excluded
from the class by the court. Such forbearance to enforce an agreement to arbitrate shall not constitute a waiver
of any rights under this Agreement except to the extent stated herein.

15. SEVERABILITY.

Any term or provision of this Agreement which is invalid or unenforceable in any jurisdiction shall, as to such
jurisdiction, be ineffective to the extent of such invalidity or unenforceability without rendering invalid or
unenforceable the remaining terms or provisions of this Agreement or affecting the validity or enforceability
of any of the terms or provisions of this Agreement in any other jurisdiction.

inside or outside of Guam, for a period of twenty (20) years from the effective date of this special qualifying
certificate ("Special QC"). This Special QC may be renewed by applying to the Guam Economic
Development Authority ("GEDA") for additional periods of twenty (20) years at the conclusion of the first
or subsequent periods as long as the Guam-based Trust remains in good standing under the laws of Guam
and under the rules and regulations of GEDA. The taxable income of the Guam-based Trust shall be computed
generally in the same manner of an individual in which the deductions and credits allowed to an individual are
also allowed to the Guam-based Trust, as provided in section 641(b) of the tax code and the exceptions
thereto. For purposes of sections 641 and 935 of the Internal Revenue Code and of the Guam Territorial
income tax, the Guam-based Trust shall be treated as an individual who is a citizen of the United States but a
resident of Guam.

Rebate of income tax withheld on dividends; renewal
[§58128.6(b), QC Law]
§1.03. The Non-Resident Beneficiary shall be entitled to a rebate of one hundred percent (100%) of the
income tax withheld from them on the payments or distributions made by the Guam-based Trust, for a period
of twenty (20) consecutive years from the effective date of the Special QC, provided, the payments or
distributions were/are subject to withholding tax. This period of rebate for the Non-Resident Beneficiary may
be renewed for additional periods of twenty (20) years at the conclusion of the first or subsequent periods so
long as the Guam-based Trust remains in good standing under the laws of Guam and under the rules and
regulations of GEDA. 6

THIS TRUST AGREEMENT is made on the day of October ,2014, by and
between HO SANG EUN, residing in, Guam (the "Grantor"), and HUI JU EUN, his wife who is
residing with the Grantor, (the "Trustec").

ARTICLE 1
CREATION OF TRUST: IRREVOCABILITY OF TRUST

(A) Creation of Trust. The Grantor hereby creates a separate trust for the benefit of
each of his currently living children, and intends to create a separate trust for the benefit of each
child who may hereafter be born to or adopted by the Grantor. The Grantor intends that transfers
to each trust shall qualify for the gift tax annual exclusion under Section 2503(b) of the Internal
Revenue Code,

(B) Transfer of Initial Contribution. The Grantor hereby transfers to the Trustees
the Initial Contribution with respect to the trusts for the benefit of each of his currently living
children. The Trustees accept and acknowledge receipt of the Initial Contribution, and agree to
hold it and all additional property received and accepted by them in trust, and to invest, manage
and distribute such property in accordance with the provisions of this trust agreement (the
"Agreement"). The Grantor does not and shall not retain any right, title or interest in or to any
property transferred to a trust hereunder at any time. All property transferred is the separate
property of Grantor, which may have acquired its separate character as a result of his interest in
community property being severed and transmuted into separate property immediately before
such transfer.

(C) Identification of Trust Agreement. This Agreement may be referred to as "THE
EUN FAMILY INVESTMENT TRUST AGREEMENT", and the separate trust created under
this Agreement for the benefit of each child of the Grantor may be referred to as "THE EUN
FAMILY 2014 TRUST f/b/o [CHILD'S NAME]",

(D) Trusts Irrevocable. This Agreement and the trusts hereunder shall be
irrevocable. The Grantor shall have no right or power in any capacity, whether alone or in
conjunction with others, to alter, amend, revoke or terminate any trust hereunder or any terms of
this Agreement, in whole or in part.

ARTICLE II
FAMILY MEMBERS: DEFINED TERMS

(A) Grantor's Wife. The Grantor is married to HUI EUN ("HUI"). For all purposes
of this Agreement, references to "the Grantor's wife" are to HUI without regard to whether the
Grantor and HUI are living together or married to each other at any time.

(B) Grantor's Children. The Grantor has three (3) children, JANE JTYOUNG EUN,
born March 8, 1997, JUSTIN JINHYUK EUN born October 5, 1991 and JUNGMIN CLAIRE

2
===== PAGE 3 =====
EUN, born July 16, 1994. References to the Grantor's children and descendants shall be applied
in accordance with Article XIII(A)(5).

(C) Defined Terms. The definition of each defined term is given in Article XIII(A) or

where the term first appears. Capitalized terms are usually defined terms.
ARTICLE III
THE EUN FAMILY INVESTMENT TRUSTS

(A) Child's Trust. The Trustees shall hold all Additions with respect to a designated
child of the Grantor (the "Child") and any property passing to a Child upon the termination of
any trust under this Agreement in trust upon the following terms:

[08] No distributions shall be made hereunder before January 1, 2017.
Thereafter distributions are permitted as follows, PROVIDED that the Trustee shall be under no
obligation to make any distribution under this Section (A) or Article III.

(2) The Trustees shall pay to such one or more of the Child and the Child's
descendants living from time to time so much of the net income and principal as the Independent
Trustees, in their discretion, determine, giving primary consideration to the Child's interests.

3) Following the death of the survivor of the Grantor and the Grantor's wife
the TRUSTEE shall pay to, or apply for the benefit of, such child so much or all of the net
income and principal of the trust as the TRUSTEE, in its discretion, deems necessary for such
child’s health, education, maintenance and support. . Any income not so distributed shall be
added to, and thereafter dealt with as part of, the principal of such trust.

(B) Distributions from Retirement Plans. With regard to any Individual Retirement
Account or pension plan (“Retirement Plans”) payable to this Trust, in addition to the principal
distributions required under subparagraphs (a) and (b) herein, the TRUSTEE shall, until such
child dies or attains the age of sixty five (65) years, withdraw the required minimum distribution
from the Retirement Plans, determined pursuant to IRC Section 401(a)(9) and the regulations
promulgated thereunder, and distribute such withdrawal to, or apply for the benefit of, such
child. After such child attains the age of sixty five (65) years, the TRUSTEE shall withdraw
from the Retirement Plans and distribute to such child the required minimum distributions and
such other amount as requested by the beneficiary in writing.

(C) Limitation on Trust Distributions. NOTWITHSTANDING ANYTHING TO
THE CONTRARY, under no circumstance may any TRUSTEE make any distribution in
accordance with this section that would discharge the TRUSTEE’s legal obligation, including
the obligation of support, toward such child.

(D) Upon Child's Death. If not terminated sooner, each Child's Trust shall terminate
upon the Child's death, and the Trustees shall pay the remaining principal as the Child appoints
by exercise of a special testamentary power of appointment as defined in Article VI(A)(1),
and/or a general testamentary power of appointment, if any, conferred pursuant to Article VI(B).
The Trustees shall pay the remaining principal not effectively appointed to the then living

3
===== PAGE 4 =====
descendants of the Child or, if no such descendant is then living, to the Grantor's then living
descendants.

(E) Tax Consequences of Distributions. Without limiting the Independent Trustees’
discretion or implying that tax considerations should take precedence over other considerations,
the Grantor requests but does not direct that the Independent Trustees take into account the
generation-skipping transfer tax consequences in exercising discretion over distributions from
trusts under this Article.

(F) Discretionary Distribution May Be in Further Trust. Property that may, in the
discretion of the Independent Trustees, be distributed to a descendant of the Child may instead,
in the discretion of the Independent Trustees, be distributed to and held by the Trustees in a
Protective Trust of which such descendant is the Beneficiary,

ARTICLE IV
PROTECTIVE TRUSTS

(A) When Descendant's Property is Held in Trust. Property passing to a
grandchild or more remote descendant of the Grantor upon the termination of any trust,
including a trust under this Article, shall not vest in or be paid to such descendant (the
"Beneficiary") but instead shall be held in a Protective Trust under this Article.

(B) Terms of Protective Trust. The Trustees shall hold all property passing to a
Protective Trust upon the following terms: The Trustees shall pay to such one or more of the
Beneficiary and the Beneficiary's descendants living from time to time so much of the net
income and principal as the Independent Trustees, in their discretion, determine, giving primary
consideration to the Beneficiary's interests.

(C) Upon Beneficiary's Death. If not terminated sooner, each Protective Trust shall
terminate upon the Beneficiary's death, and the Trustees shall pay the remaining principal as the
Beneficiary appoints by exercise of a special testamentary power of appointment as defined in
Article VI(A)(1), and/or a general testamentary power of appointment, if any, conferred
pursuant to Article VI(B). The Trustees shall pay the remaining principal not effectively
appointed to the then living descendants of the Beneficiary or, if no such descendant is then
living, to the then living descendants of the Beneficiary's Nearest Ancestor or, if no such
descendant is then living, to the Beneficiary's Nearest Ancestor.

"Nearest Ancestor" means the Beneficiary's nearest ancestor in the line of descent
beginning with (but not including) the Grantor of whom either of the following is then true: (i) a
descendant of that ancestor is then living, or (ii) that ancestor is then living.

Property that may, in the discretion of the Independent Trustees, be distributed to a
descendant of the Child may instead, in the discretion of the Independent Trustees, be distributed
to and held by the Trustees in a Protective Trust of which such descendant is the Beneficiary.
Such sequence of Protective trusts may continue without limit, other than those to avoid
perpetuities as set out in Article IV (F).

4
===== PAGE 5 =====
(D) Tax Consequences of Distributions. Without limiting the Independent Trustees’
discretion or implying that tax considerations should take precedence over other considerations,
the Grantor requests but does not direct that the Independent Trustees take into account the
generation-skipping transfer tax consequences in exercising discretion over distributions from
trusts under this Article.

(E) Discretionary Distributions May Be in Further Trust. Property that may, in
the discretion of the Independent Trustees, be distributed to a descendant of the Beneficiary of a
Protective Trust may instead, in the discretion of the Independent Trustees, be distributed to and
held by the Trustees in a Protective Trust of which such descendant is the Beneficiary.

(F) Application of Rule Against Perpetuities. Notwithstanding any contrary
provision of this Agreement, each trust under this Article still in existence upon the expiration of
any Perpetuities Period applicable to the trust shall thereupon terminate. Upon termination of a
trust pursuant to this Paragraph, the Trustees shall pay the remaining principal to the
Beneficiary.

ARTICLE V
REMOTE DISPOSITIONS

If any part of the remaining principal of any trust under this Agreement is not effectively
disposed of under the other provisions of this Agreement, such property shall be disposed of as
follows:

(A) Alternate Beneficiaries. Such property shall be divided into as many equal
shares as are effectively disposed of below and such shares shall be paid to the GRANTOR ’s
then living heirs at law, determined in accordance with the statutes of Guam governing the
intestate distribution of separate property which are in effect on the date of the GRANTOR’S
death.

(B) Time of Determination. If a distribution is to be made upon the termination
of any trust hereunder, the determination of the heirs at law of the GRANTOR shall be made as
if such person had died immediately upon such termination.

ARTICLE VI
POWERS OF APPOINTMENT

(A) Powers of Appointment. All testamentary powers of appointment conferred
pursuant to this Agreement are subject to the following provisions:

(1) A special power of appointment shall not be exercisable by the Child or

her own favor or in favor of his or her creditors or estate or the creditors of his or her estate.
Otherwise, a special power may be exercised in favor of any person and any Qualified Charity,
whether outright or in trust (including any split-interest trust), provided that if a descendant of the
Grantor is then living, a special power shall be exercisable only in favor of (i) persons who are
among a class consisting of the Grantor's descendants and any spouse, widow or widower of any
of the Grantor's descendants (including a Donee's spouse), and (ii) any Qualified Charity,

of support;

(B) Trust Administrative Provisions. In the administration of all trusts hereunder:

(1) The Trustees may act primarily in the interests of the current beneficiaries

regard to the interests of subsequent beneficiaries or remaindermen or any rules of trust law
which may require impartiality as among such interests, and the interests of all subsequent
beneficiaries or remaindermen are subordinate to the exercise of such powers. The Grantor
intends the Trustees to exercise liberally their discretionary powers over income and principal in
favor of beneficiaries of the trust in the absence of affirmative reasons (including tax reasons) for
retention of income or principal or the continuation of the trust. The Trustees may, but shall not
be required to, inquire into or take into account the other income or resources of any beneficiary
or the obligation of any person to support any beneficiary.

(2) The Trustees may make discretionary payments of income or principal in
equal or unequal amounts and at any time and from time to time may exclude any one or more
beneficiaries from any such payment. Any net income of any trust which is not required to be
distributed and which is not distributed within sixty-five (65) days after the close of the taxable
year of the trust in which such income was received shall be added to principal.

3) In applying income or principal for a beneficiary under the age of twenty-
one (21) years or under other legal disability, the Trustees may take into consideration that such
beneficiary might otherwise be a financial burden to his or her guardian or parent or the person
with whom he or she may be living, and accordingly, may pay from such beneficiary's trust an
appropriate share of the expenses of the guardian, parent, or other person in maintaining the
home in which the beneficiary and any other persons reside and other related expenses.

(4) If the value of any trust is at any time of such a modest amount that the
continued administration of the trust is not in the opinion of the Trustees economically
reasonable, the Independent Trustees, in their discretion, may terminate such trust and distribute

under Section 2055(a), and which is described in Section 2055(a) and Section 1361(e)(1)(A)(),
All of said Section references are to the Internal Revenue Code.

(20) "Residential Property": any interests in real property (together with
buildings, fixtures, and improvements thereon), condominium units (including common areas),
or cooperative apartments (together with proprietary leases and shares of stock relating thereto)
used by a beneficiary under this Agreement for residential or vacation purposes.

(21) "S Corporation"; the same meaning as in Section 1361 of the Internal
Revenue Code.

(22) "spouse"; in relation to any individual, the person who is married to and
not legally separated from such individual at the relevant time.

defined by law, including automobiles, household furniture and furnishings, books, photographs,
works of art, apparel, jewelry and other articles of household use or ornament, but excluding
cash, coins without numismatic value, property used solely in or constituting part of the

(24) "Transferor": any person, including the Grantor, who makes or has made
an Addition to a trust hereunder or any prior trust from which such trust is derived.

(26) "Trust Beneficiary": with respect to each trust hereunder, a current or
successor income beneficiary or Presumptive Remainderman of such trust.

(B) Construction of Terms. In construing this Agreement:

[(}] If any beneficiary dies within ninety (90) days after the date on which he
or she becomes entitled to any property interest under this Agreement other than a Power of
Withdrawal (whether outright or in trust), such beneficiary shall be deemed to have died prior to
such date.

(2) Property payable to the descendants of any person (including the Grantor)
shall be paid to such descendants per stirpes, that is, such property shall be divided into as many
equal shares as there are children of such person who are then living or who have died leaving
then living descendants. Each living child shall be allocated one such share, and any share in
respect of a deceased child shall be divided further among such child's then living descendants in
the same manner,

3) For purposes of this Agreement, a person shall be deemed "mentally
incapacitated" upon certification in writing by two (2) physicians licensed to practice in the state
of such person's residence to the effect that such person has sustained substantial and significant
loss of mental capacity, whether or not a court of competent jurisdiction has declared him or her
to be mentally incompetent, mentally ill or in need of a guardian, conservator or similar
fiduciary, Such written certification shall be filed with the records of any trust affected by such
person's incapacity. The determination of a return of mental capacity of any person who has been
deemed mentally incapacitated pursuant to this provision shall be established in the same
manner, provided that the physicians who make such subsequent determination need not be the
same physicians who made the earlier determination. During the period that a person is deemed
mentally incapacitated, he or she shall be treated for purposes of this Agreement as if under a
legal disability.

[C)] References to a provision, section, chapter or rule of any federal or state
statute or regulation are to such provision, section, chapter or rule as amended from time to time

law of a jurisdiction other than a state of the United States (such as the District of Columbia or a

(6) References to property paid to a beneficiary shall include property applied
for such beneficiary's benefit. The duty or power to pay property to a beneficiary shall include
the power to apply the property for the benefit of the beneficiary,

(7) Titles, captions and headings in this Agreement are solely for convenience
of reference and shall not affect the construction of any provision of this Agreement.
